title: Edge Aggregator: adaptive enrichment & flow-control for inference KPIs
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem: Edge collectors producing inference KPIs are bursty and high-cardinality. Downstream Prometheus remote_write endpoints and the central OTLP pipeline see spikes that cause increased tail latency and sample drops during tenant bursts. We also have inconsistent label sets from different SDK versions (route vs model vs tenant labels) which prevents tenant-level rollups and accurate per-route billing/latency SLOs.

Goal: Ship a lightweight edge aggregator that performs three coordinated responsibilities: (1) canonicalize/enrich metric labels according to our canonical schema, (2) perform deterministic adaptive sampling for known high-cardinality dimensions to preserve statistical fidelity, and (3) provide flow-control/backpressure behavior (buffer, shed, or apply token-bucket backpressure) when downstream write latency or queue depth exceeds configured SLOs. The component must support both Prometheus remote_write and OTLP export modes and be deployable as a small sidecar on Dedicated/Private nodes and as an optional proxy in Hosted edge tiers.

Non-goals: This is not a full-scale tenant aggregator with multi-tenant isolation or billing reconciliation; longer-term deduplication & enrichment heavy-lifting remains in the central metric fabric. We will not change the canonical metric schema in this ticket.

Design summary: The edge aggregator runs as a single-threaded fast-path in Rust, exposing an OTLP/Prometheus intake. It uses a short-lived hot cache of canonical label mappings (configurable TTL & versioned) and a small deterministic sampler keyed by (tenant, route, model, signature). Sampling decisions are deterministic per time-window so downstream rollups remain stable. Flow-control modes include: (A) buffer-to-disk with max size + priority eviction, (B) adaptive shed by pre-configured policies (shed least-important labels/metrics first), and (C) token-bucket backpressure that returns 429 to upstream agents (opt-in for older SDKs).

Plan: 1) Proto-impl: implement schema normalizer and deterministic sampler; smoke test locally against synthetic bursts. 2) Add flow-control policies and a simple on-disk buffer. 3) Integrate dual-mode export adapters: OTLP exporter (gRPC) and Prometheus remote_write. 4) Create e2e test harness that replays recorded edge traces (from incident 2026-02-14) to validate no-drops under steady-state and graceful shedding under spike. 5) Canary deploy to small Dedicated pool, monitor KPIs, then roll to Hosted edge.

Tradeoffs: Doing enrichment at edge reduces central compute and network egress but increases CPU & memory consumption at edge nodes. Deterministic sampling preserves variance but can still bias small-sample tenants—will document in SDK notes. Returning 429s is invasive; default will prefer shedding/buffering and 429 only if explicitly enabled for a tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical label normalization applied to incoming metric envelopes with config-driven mappings
Deterministic sampling reduces cardinality for target dimensions by at least 70% on synthetic burst profiles while preserving 95th/99th quantile estimates within 10%
At 2x baseline ingest bursts, downstream remote_write latency remains within SLO (P95 < 300ms) due to buffering or shedding behavior
Dual-mode export validated: messages successfully appear in central OTLP pipeline and in Prometheus remote_write receiver in test cluster
Automated e2e replay test covering buffer persistence, crash recovery, and policy-driven shedding
Canary rollout plan with rollback signal defined and dashboards created

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Edge CPU increase may push node resource limits. Mitigation: provide autoscaling knobs and default light mode; add admission controller to avoid scheduling where insufficient resources.

Risk: Sampling introduces billing variance for small tenants. Mitigation: expose sampling whitelist/blacklist and document expected behavior; preserve raw traces for top N tenants for billing reconciliation.
Risk: Disk buffer corruption on crash. Mitigation: use append-only format with checksum and recovery on startup; limit default disk usage to 50MB per instance.
